The code snippet calls `listeners.toArray(new ConnectionListener[listeners.size()])`. The `listeners` is likely a `Vector<ConnectionListener>` or similar collection. The context shows that the array passed is a freshly created `ConnectionListener` array of exactly the same size as the collection. According to the API javadoc, two exceptions are declared: ArrayStoreException and NullPointerException. 

- NullPointerException: occurs if the given array is null. Here, the array is explicitly created with `new ConnectionListener[listeners.size()]`, so it is never null. Thus, the condition for NullPointerException is fully avoided.
- ArrayStoreException: occurs if the runtime type of the array is not a supertype of the runtime type of every element in the Vector. Since the elements are presumably of type `ConnectionListener` (or a subtype), and the array is of type `ConnectionListener[]`, the array type is a supertype (same type) of the elements. Therefore, this exception is also avoided.

No other exceptions are declared. Both exceptions are avoided in the calling context.
